output.name: Naskel
output.myth: Long ago a pale tree came up out of the Unflown on a south wind. It had no leaves, only the trunk, and the sea had worn it smooth as bone. Tavo the Gale saw it, laughed, and flung it north over the rim of the water, where it should have fallen. It did not fall. Orrun felt it knock along his back under the waves and said nothing, which is how you know Orrun is annoyed. Sil saw it turning in the moonlight and took it for a kite, and followed until the spray took it. It goes round the Lamp Road with its broken top pointed at home. It passes Skelra, the Split Oar, and comes near the Long Night Fire on the longest night, while Sekar, who swam under floes, watches it from the north. It looks down on Tirun, the Upturned Hull, which came home keel-up with eleven names gone. My mother says Mesal the knot-lamp keeps an eye on it. If you find a pale log on the beach, do not burn it. Something on it is still counting its way back.
output.finding: Find Skelra, the Split Oar, about two and a half fists north-east of home on the Lamp Road, then look one hand-span further along that road toward the north-west for a pale, smooth log with its broken top pointed at the islands.
